children: By Nelson Bocanegra and Carlos Vargas

Colombia's government plans to swap some of its local debt in September, October and November as it adjusts this year's budget after sharply increasing its borrowing needs, several market makers told Reuters on Monday.
The comments came after a meeting with Cesar Arias, the finance ministry's public credit director, who declined to comment.

The debt swaps, expected at the end of each month, would involve different types of local government securities, including fixed-rate bonds, inflation-linked bonds and short-term notes, three market makers said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
Such swaps allow governments to replace existing debt with new debt, often to manage repayment schedules, reduce pressure on near-term financing needs or improve borrowing conditions.

Colombia last week revised its fiscal outlook in a move that alarmed investors. The government raised its fiscal deficit forecast for 2026 to 7.2% of gross domestic product from 5.3%, and for 2027 to 9.4% from 4.5%.
Those new projections are far above the targets set by the previous government.
Under the revised plans, Colombia will borrow an additional 35 trillion pesos ($11.13 billion) this year.
"For now, it is just a plan to get through 2026, which is understandable," one market maker said.
More details on upcoming local bond auctions and other debt management operations are expected on Friday, the sources added.

title: Colombia to swap local government debt as borrowing needs rise, market makers say
